label: echoed digit 1 as input at the first or second copy step (short sequences)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the input is the digit 1, i.e. the model fed back its own just-emitted 1. Almost all of it (93% of mass) is at recall_idx 1, the step right after <DEL> when orig(0) was 1. Here activation is strongest (up to the max, about 3.2) for short sequences (L=4-5). It weakens as L grows and is mostly absent at L=9. A weaker secondary mode (7% of mass, activation around 0.0-0.4 of max) is at recall_idx 2 when orig(1) was 1, and only for short L (6 or less). Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, on any other token, or on a fed-back 1 at later copy positions (recall_idx 3 or more). The magnitude tracks how early in the copy phase the 1 appears and how short the sequence is. It does not depend on the token being output next.

issues: Main claims hold on the test split. The feature only fires in the copy phase and only when the input is 1. The recall_idx 1 mode is nearly perfect: precision 0.998 for L<=7 and 0.982 for L<=8, holding 92% of mass. At L=9 precision is 0.19 with 0.3% of mass, so 'mostly absent' is fair. recall_idx>=3 holds about 0.1% of mass.

Small systematic false-positive class: at recall_idx 2 with L=3 (the last copy step) the feature never fires, with precision 0.002 over 434 predicted steps. The predicate's L<=6 condition includes this case. Requiring L>=4 lifts test F1 from 0.891 to 0.900.

The recall_idx 2 mode is noisy: precision 0.50 at L=4, 0.83 at L=5 and 0.53 at L=6. Nothing I checked explains the rest: whether first_tok is a digit, letter or vowel, correct, in_count, or next_out. The explanation's '7% of mass' is right, but this mode is 26% of active steps by count. It is low-magnitude, so it reads as threshold noise rather than a missing variable.
The test misses list only weak activations (0.5% of mass) scattered across L=9 and recall_idx 3. No systematic missed class.
